# Automatic differentiation is a testing problem

## Nobody can tell you which backend to use

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="55%"}
- Six configurations in CI. ForwardDiff, ReverseDiff on tape, Enzyme
  forward and reverse, Mooncake forward and reverse. Each gets its own
  job, its own badge and its own Codecov flag
- `CensoredDistributions.jl` is green on all six, with one declared
  broken scenario on each Enzyme direction. Both are the same
  `convolve_series` case on a stacked
  `IntervalCensored{Truncated{PrimaryCensored}}`
- `ComposedDistributions.jl` fails all six on `main`, as of 10 August
:::
::: {.column width="45%"}
- DifferentiationInterface tells you about a function. Turing tells you
  what Turing tests. Nothing tells you about a model assembled from five
  packages that each tested on their own
- The one public per-backend table for a probabilistic programming
  stack, `TuringLang/ADTests`, was archived in June

::: {.attribution}
Declared broken scenarios in
[CensoredDistributions.jl#889][cd889], read from `test/ADFixtures` on
`main` · last `AD` run on `main` green 2026-08-05 there and red
2026-08-07 in `ComposedDistributions.jl` ·
[TuringLang/ADTests][adtests], archived 2026-06-15.
:::
:::
::::

## What we added on top of DifferentiationInterfaceTest

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="55%"}
- DifferentiationInterfaceTest works per function and per package. We
  added a registry where a package declares which scenarios are broken
  on which backend, and `check_broken` re-runs them, so a stale
  declaration gets flagged
- One list generates the CI matrix, the Codecov flags, the README badges
  and the published support table, so the docs cannot drift from CI
- `gamma_inc` and `beta_inc` carry no AD rules, so we hand-wrote those
  derivatives. `ScoringRules.jl` hit the same two from scratch
:::
::: {.column width="45%"}
::: {.callout-important}
Without this, building a model is a custom job with a lot of iteration.
That is not realistic in an outbreak.
:::

- Mooncake returns a wrong gradient when a Gamma shape lands on exactly
  1.0, through a missing rule for `xlogy`. Not an error. A wrong number
- We found it and reduced it to three lines. Our bot then filed it
  upstream by mistake and we withdrew it, so it is still not reported.
  `EpiAwareADTools.jl` holds the workaround in the meantime

::: {.attribution}
Reduced example and the unfiled report in
[ComposedDistributions.jl#99][cd99].
:::
:::
